why: The HC-SR04 ranges to 2 m in any light, about 10 body lengths. The robot can then cruise the dark corridor near full speed and steer around obstacles without touching them, saving at least the 40 s of back-offs plus the speed cap. The camera is ruled out because its IR LED lights only 0.12 m in the dark, and the lidar is not provided. Cost: $2.50, 2 days lead time.

Wheels can't climb an edge higher than their radius (4.5 cm at most), so no wheel radius reaches 5.5 cm, and a 9 cm wheel only just matches the trench. Tracks with idler height 7 cm meet the 5.5 cm step on their front run. A 24 cm contact length bridges 0.45×24 = 10.8 cm, more than the 9.1 cm trench. Two 24 cm tracks give roughly 150–200 cm² of contact, so about 0.35 kPa and under 0.5 cm of sinkage. This avoids both reasons last round's version was refused. The tub is 24 cm long, which fits a 24 cm track. The NiMH pack is 6 cells: 7.2 V running, 8.4 V charged, under the N20's 9 V limit. Six cells instead of four give 1.5× the speed and force, which makes up for the tracks' 1.8 cm sprocket and having only two motors. I estimate about 0.65 m/s top speed and about 15 N of force, and 12.2 Wh usable energy covers the 5 km lawn. Inner width 10 keeps the robot narrow for the bedroom. Ride height 3 puts the tub top at 7 cm, under the track's 8.5 cm. The 8 cells needed are already in the lab. The only purchase is the $14 track kit, with 4 days of lead time.
